You are a research assistant filling ONE knowledge gap for a travel catalog.
Rules you must follow:
- You discover sources yourself through the search tool. There is no list of preferred sites.
- You only PROPOSE claims. You never decide that a claim is true; a separate grounding step verifies everything.
- Every claim must quote text copied EXACTLY from a document you fetched in this session (same words). No quote, no claim.
- Never state coordinates, identifiers or geometry. Name places as the source names them.
- Street geometry or a map listing does not make a place relevant for tourists; the quote must say why it matters.
- Do not rely on your own knowledge as evidence.

Gap: Find neighbourhoods/areas of Buenos Aires that are relevant to travellers interested in "theme:food".
Permitted claim types: RELEVANT_FOR.
  RELEVANT_FOR: {"claimType":"RELEVANT_FOR","subject":"<area or place name>","themes":["history"]}
  NOTABLE_WITHIN: {"claimType":"NOTABLE_WITHIN","subject":"<place>","area":"<area>","themes":["food"]}
  WALKING_CORRIDOR: {"claimType":"WALKING_CORRIDOR","subject":"<street>","area":"<area named by the source, optional>","from":"<start, optional>","to":"<end, optional>","themes":["history"]}
  Each claim also has "authorityClass" (your guess about the publisher, optional) and
  "evidence":[{"doc":"<doc id like d1>","quote":"<exact sentence from that doc>"}].
Remaining budget: 3 steps, 3 searches, 3 fetches.

That’s why I’ve organized this guide by neighborhood. You’ll discover the best neighborhoods and what makes them great, then I include a list of my favorite hotels and hostels in each for all budgets. TLDR: My Top Recommendations Looking for a quick list of the best places to stay in Buenos Aires, without the fluff? Here are my favorite hotels for every budget: BEST OVERALL | Home Hotel in Palermo Hollywood BEST BOUTIQUE HOTELS | Jardin Escondido by Coppola & Magnolia , both in Palermo Soho BEST LUXURY | Park Hyatt in Recoleta BEST HOSTELS | Che Juan in Centro, Viajero in San Telmo or Casa Caravan in Palermo BEST AIRBNB/VRBO | This apartment is modern, clean and the highest rated in Palermo Where To Stay in Buenos Aires by Neighborhood Ok, let’s finally get to the point, shall we? Here are the best places to stay in Buenos Aires by barrio. Buenos Aires is the epitome of urban sprawl. There are 48 neighborhoods plus suburbs on all sides. A third of the country calls the great Buenos Aires area home. It’s a lot. So which area is best for you? Let’s find out. You may also be interested in: The Best Things to do in Buenos Aires Microcentro: Downtown (Montserrat/San Cristobal) Downtown at a glance : A tempting place to stay due to its central location around the sights, but also a hectic business district that is loud at night, lacking the charm of other neighborhoods. Good for those with very short stays (think 1-2 days, you want to see the hits and fast). I’m starting with the downtown neighborhoods all looped together (Microcentro/Montserrat/San Cristobal), because I have strong opinions about it. Due to its central location by the obelisk and other main sights, the conglomerate of hotel chains and tango theaters… it’s tempting to stay here. It feels logical, I know. But I would recommend against that, for most of you. Microcentro is the city’s business district so it’s a bit dead at night and on weekends. It can feel less safe and while it has great dining options for lunch – read: business crowd – it’s less charming for dinner. Instead, I’d stay somewhere like Palermo (or other options mentioned below), where you’ll have charming cobblestone streets, canopies of trees, and more dining options than you could dream of. But when SHOULD you stay downtown? If you only have one or two short days in the city, then yes, I would stay downtown. You really do need to see the sites as quickly and efficiently as possible. But I would stay on Avenida de Mayo instead of on 9 de Julio. It is just as central but much more charming than massive 9 de Julio. Where to Stay in El Centro Buenos Aires Marriott | $$$$ | If you’re dead set in staying the heart of it all by the Obelisco, the absolute best option is the Marriott. It has a clean style and is luxurious, the roof top pool is the epitome of luxury, and rooms offer views of the Teatro Colon and the Obelisco. Tango de Mayo | $$ | Charming boutique hotel right on Avenida de Mayo. It’s next door to Palacio Barolo, a block from the Congressional palace and a short walk to Plaza de Mayo. The roof bar, Domo, is a wonderful spot to unwind at sunset. Che Juan | $ | Always the most highly recommended hostel among travelers in my FB group , it is modern and stylish, it’s very central to the sights and San Telmo. Parla Hostel | $ | Popular hostel downtown, very social with friendly, outgoing staff. Great for solo travelers looking to meet up with fellow backpackers. Palermo Soho Soho at a glance: Widely regarded as the best place to stay and I agree. Best boutique hotel ($$$$) BE Jardin Escondido Modern boutique hotel ($$) Palermitano by DON Cozy boutique hotel ($$) Magnolia Boutique Hotel Best Soho hostel ($) Malevo Murana Hostel Palermo Soho Palermo holds the trophy as the best area to stay in Buenos Aires as a whole. While downtown is a cacophony of noise and activity day and night, the leafy streets of Palermo are a quieter and charming respite. By basing yourself here you’ll be next to the city’s best cafes and restaurants as well, making breakfast and dinner near your hotel a breeze. There are no chains here. In Palermo you’ll find apartments to rent , charming boutique hotels like Magnolia or BE Jardin , and stylish hostels like plant-based concept house Casa Caravan . Palermo is overflowing with street art , restaurants, cafes and bars as well as some of the best shopping in Buenos Aires. Soho is home to award-winning Don Julio & Fogon Asado , El Preferido de Palermo and the Sherpa Food Tour. The most active areas of Soho (cafes/art/etc) are the blocks surrounding Plaza Armenia and Plaza Serrano. But is Palermo too far? This is a concern I hear often from readers. I insist, it isn’t. With a taxi or the subway you can be downtown in 15-20 minutes. Having the peace of the leafy streets and sidewalk cafes at your door for breakfast and happy hour/dinner will make your stay far more enjoyable. Where to Stay in Palermo Soho Read all about Soho in my Palermo Soho neighborhood guide . BE Jardin Escondido by Coppola | $$$$ | Charming boutique hotel in a historic home. Impeccably decorated rooms surround an oasis of a garden. And yes, it’s owned by that Coppola. Ideal for couples. Miravida Boutique Hotel & Wine Bar | $$$ | Housed in a historic building in the heart of Soho. Rooms are cozy with dark, decadent colors. With a wine bar in the lobby and wine tastings in their cellar , what more do you need? Magnolia Boutique Hotel | $$ | On Julian Alvarez it is technically not in Soho proper but it is just 3 blocks away. It is cozy and you’ll feel at home. The surrounding blocks are home to great restaurants and cafes. Casa Caravan | $$ | A modern plant-based hostel, you can rent private rooms (moderately priced) or a bed in a dorm. Rooms are stylish and the pool is a green oasis (ideal for hot summer days). They have regular activities like weekend yoga or vegan asados.
